transcript:
Header: 2025-09-03 15:30 PDT | Duration: ~75m | Attendees: Samira P., Ethan C., Priya R. (Redwood) — Dr. Marco R., Leah C., Ibrahim A., Nora K. (Ember)

Summary:
- Kickoff scoping for a 4-week POC focused on quality evaluation and benchmark baselining for Ember's clinical summarization workload.
- Agreed on success criteria (accuracy/precision targets, hallucination ceilings, format fidelity), dataset size, and timeline for pilot runs.

Topics Covered:
- Success criteria and pass/fail thresholds
- Workload sizing (QPS, batch shape, sequence lengths)
- Golden prompts and rubric design
- Regression tests and hallucination/format checks
- Scoring approach (automated + human eval mix)
- Logistics: infra mode (dedicated vs hosted), data controls, timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's do a quick round of intros and then we can jump into the evaluation playbook for the POC.
[00:07] Dr. Marco Ruiz: thanks, Marco here — Head of ML at Ember. We're focused on clinical note summarization and extraction, so quality is like top priority.
[00:16] Leah Chen: Leah — eng manager, we'll own data prep and run the tests with Redwood.
[00:20] Ethan Cole: Ethan from Redwood, I'll lead the benchmark setup and perf baselining.
[00:24] Ibrahim Al-Sayeed: Ibrahim, product, mainly timeline and success metrics.
[00:28] Nora Kim: Nora, privacy/compliance, quick note: Ember must keep PHI inside our VPC and encrypted at rest, will talk about that later.
[00:35] Samira Patel: noted, we'll cover deployment modes. quick high level: four week POC, split into 1) dataset ingestion & golden prompts, 2) baseline runs + perf, 3) regression and hallucination testing, 4) final scorecard and recommendations. sound right?
[00:47] Dr. Marco Ruiz: yes, though we might extend if initial runs need more iteration.
[00:51] Ethan Cole: one thing to flag: our recommended baseline includes both hosted Redwood API and Redwood Dedicated in-customer VPC runs if you want to compare latency/cost tradeoffs.
[00:59] Leah Chen: what do you need from us to start?
[01:03] Ethan Cole: sample datasets (3 types): short encounter notes, long discharge summaries, and structured lab-obs pairs. ideally n=40-200 docs per set; one labelled subset of 50 rows for hallucination checks.
[01:15] Dr. Marco Ruiz: we can provide those. question on golden prompts: do you define them or we co-author?
[01:21] Priya Rao: we usually co-author — Redwood drafts initial golden prompt set (5-10 per task) and you iterate. the goal is to converge on 'golden prompts' that represent expected style, required fields, and allowed abbreviations.
[01:33] Ibrahim Al-Sayeed: ok, and how do you score items? precision/recall? ROUGE?
[01:37] Ethan Cole: good question — we use a hybrid rubric. automated metrics (ROUGE-L, BERTScore) for broad catch, plus targeted format checks (regex for ICD codes, date formats) and hallucination detection heuristics. then a 20% human eval slice for clinical correctness and safety. final score is weighted: 40% automated quality, 40% hallucination/format pass-rate, 20% human score.
[01:56] Dr. Marco Ruiz: what are pass thresholds?
[01:58] Samira Patel: propose initial thresholds: ROUGE-L > 0.45 on summaries, BERTScore > 0.80, hallucination rate < 5% on labelled subset, format compliance > 95%, human judge average >= 4/5 on criticality and accuracy. these are negotiable.
[02:15] Leah Chen: hallucination rate <5% seems tight but fair for production. how do you detect hallucinations automatically?
[02:21] Ethan Cole: we run entity cross-checks — extracted entities against source text; for clinical facts we match against structured fields when available. plus a heuristics engine flags halluc/unsupported claims for human review. it's not perfect but helps triage.
[02:33] Nora Kim: from compliance POV we need the audit trail for those checks; can Redwood provide logs and signed timestamps?
[02:38] Priya Rao: yes, Redwood Console exports trace-level logs per request and we can pin retention for the POC; we'll include sample log schema in the security packet.
[02:46] Ibrahim Al-Sayeed: about workload sizing, our production target is 150 qps during peak for inference, but POC runs can be a steady stream to simulate concurrency — what's a recommended test harness?
[02:57] Ethan Cole: for the POC we'll simulate a scaled-down shape: 5 client workers with bursts to emulate 20-40 concurrent streams and token lengths matching discharge notes (~2k tokens). We'll instrument tail-latency (p95/p99) and throughput. If you want throughput-level comparisons we'll run Dedicated with reserved GPUs vs Hosted and capture cost per 1k tokens.
[03:17] Leah Chen: token length ~2k — that'll change kernel selection, yep?
[03:21] Ethan Cole: exactly — the runtime will pick different kernels and KV cache behavior matters. we'll note recommended model variants and quantization for Ember's sequence length distribution.
[03:30] Dr. Marco Ruiz: for regression tests — we want to ensure no quality regressions across model updates. what's the automated plan?
[03:36] Priya Rao: we use a golden prompt regression harness: baseline outputs stored as canonical responses; we run nightly batch comparisons, compute diffs on structured fields, and flag regressions exceeding configurable thresholds. also we maintain 'golden' examples that must pass exactly (format and key facts) — these act as canaries.
[03:52] Leah Chen: do those golden examples tolerate minor phrasing changes?
[03:55] Ethan Cole: yes, canonical check is hierarchical: structured keys and required facts must match; free-text may have similarity thresholds (e.g., embedding similarity > 0.92).
[04:06] Dr. Marco Ruiz: how do you handle false positives in the regression alerts? we don't want alert fatigue.
[04:10] Priya Rao: we'll tune thresholds and create triage rules: low-severity diffs go to an auto-accept queue, medium trigger a human check, high block releases. we'll iterate during the POC.
[04:21] Ibrahim Al-Sayeed: timeline recap?
[04:23] Samira Patel: Week 0 (this week): data and golden prompt drafting. Week 1: baseline runs hosted + dedicated. Week 2: targeted hallucination/regression tests and human eval slice. Week 3: iterate and tune prompts/quantization; Week 4: final scorecard and recommendation.
[04:40] Leah Chen: human eval slice — how many labels?
[04:42] Ethan Cole: propose 200 samples across tasks (weighted to critical ones) with clinical annotators; can either be Ember annotators or Redwood-managed with NDAs.
[04:51] Nora Kim: any PHI exposure concerns if Redwood manages human eval?
[04:54] Samira Patel: if Redwood does human eval we use dedicated SSO accounts with IP restrictions, or we can run the human eval internally at Ember; option is yours. we'll include both flows in the doc.
[05:03] Dr. Marco Ruiz: scoring rubric — can we see an example?
[05:05] Ethan Cole: yes, we'll send a draft scoring sheet: numeric criteria for factuality (0-5), completeness (0-5), format (pass/fail), hallucination flag (binary) and overall accept/reject. plus a separate safety checklist for potential harmful or risky suggestions.
[05:19] Leah Chen: benchmarks — do you do cost modeling per run?
[05:21] Priya Rao: yes, we'll provide per-1k token cost for each mode (hosted vs dedicated) and expected P95 latency. we also include recommended quantization that typically reduces cost 20-40% with small quality tradeoffs.
[05:32] Ibrahim Al-Sayeed: if we find model regresses on a safety criterion how fast can you roll back?
[05:36] Samira Patel: rollbacks can be immediate to a pinned model version; our rollout policies support canary and quick automatic fallback. we'll show an example config in the playbook.
[05:46] Dr. Marco Ruiz: about the hallucination labeled subset — do you need annotations from our clinicians?
[05:50] Ethan Cole: ideally yes, Ember's clinicians label a gold 50-sample set for hallucination ground truth; Redwood can assist with annotation tooling and guidelines.
[05:58] Nora Kim: for compliance docs, send over encryption, KMS/HSM details and SOC2 extract.
[06:02] Samira Patel: we'll attach those to the next email.
[06:05] Ibrahim Al-Sayeed: logistics: who is the single point?
[06:08] Samira Patel: primary AE is Samira, SE is Ethan, Solutions Eng Priya will run eval harness. For Ember side, Marco + Leah as leads.
[06:16] Leah Chen: ok good. any blockers on our side?
[06:18] Dr. Marco Ruiz: timing — we need final exec review in 6 weeks, so POC must finish and deliverables must be aligned.
[06:25] Samira Patel: understood — we'll map deliverables to your exec timeline.
[06:28] Priya Rao: quick note: we'll include a sample bench script and a dockerized harness for local runs so you can reproduce.
[06:34] Ethan Cole: also will provide a checklist for format checks: regex examples for ICD patterns, date normalization rules, and expected JSON schema for outputs.
[06:42] Leah Chen: great, can you also include how to interpret false positives from the hallucination heuristic?
[06:46] Priya Rao: yes, we'll add a section with known heuristics, limitations, and recommended triage steps (example: when entity mention mismatch is due to coreference).
[06:55] Dr. Marco Ruiz: are there any model families you recommend for long clinical notes?
[06:59] Ethan Cole: typically we recommend [open models] with long-context support; we'll propose two variants: a higher-accuracy dense 32k-context model for summaries and a quantized faster model for extraction tasks. specifics in the playbook.
[07:10] Samira Patel: OK let's recap action items and next steps.
[07:12] Samira Patel: Redwood will: 1) deliver golden prompts and template (Ethan + Priya) by Fri 2025-09-05; 2) baseline scripts and docker harness by 2025-09-05; 3) security docs (SOC2 slice, KMS details) by 2025-09-06. Ember will: 1) provide datasets and labelled hallucination subset by 2025-09-10; 2) confirm whether Redwood will run human eval or Ember will run in-house by 2025-09-07.
[07:34] Ibrahim Al-Sayeed: can we book the 2-hour pilot walk-through for 2025-09-17?
[07:37] Samira Patel: yes I'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[07:39] Nora Kim: thanks all.
[07:40] Samira Patel: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the playbook and artifacts.

End Transcript.
